official.description_text:
Postdoc in solid-state batteries - Electrochemical and chemical characterization
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
Next leap in the battery development is expected to be the lithium solid-state batteries (SSB), allowing the replacement of the flammable organic electrolyte in Li-ion batteries with a safer and a more compact solid electrolyte. Within the framework of the Swedish governmental battery initiative COMPEL, aimed to support competence and excellence in battery research and education for the transport sector, KTH join forces with a coordinated initiative on composite SSB with seven postdoctoral positions in several disciplines, focusing on various aspects along the battery value chain, ranging from synthesis, cell assembly, characterization, modeling to scaled-up manufacturing. The 2-year postdoc project
Electrochemical properties of solid-state batteries and analysis of interactions between its different components
will be shared between Depts Chemical Engineering (Div Applied Electrochemistry) and Chemistry (Div. Applied Physical Chemistry). The project will focus on electrochemical and chemical evaluation of components and cells with materials produced in parallel postdoc projects in the initiative
.
The research aims to gain a deeper understanding of the structure / performance relationship of the developed electrolytes and interactions between the electrode materials and electrolyte, the conduction mechanism, degradation and the relationship between manufacturing process and materials properties. The analysis relies on combining electrochemical methods, such as electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, with for instance nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR), electron microscopy (SEM/TEM), Raman and in situ mass spectrometry (OLMS).
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in Electrochemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related subject with experience in electrochemistry.This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Proficiency in written and spoken English, as this will be required in day-to-day work.
Strong laboratory and instrumental skills.
Awareness of diversity and equal treatment issues with a particular focus on gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline.
Experience in solid-state batteries and well-acquainted with electrochemical characterization techniques of batteries.
Hands-on experience with material NMR and/or Raman spectroscopy.
An innovative mindset and ability to work independently.
Good collaborative skills and abilities and interest in working in a team.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.

KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. ai.summary: Postdoc in battery materials characterisation at KTH investigating electrochemical and chemical properties of solid-state battery components and cells, using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, NMR, SEM/TEM, Raman spectroscopy, and in situ mass spectrometry.

thematic_fit.rationale: Battery electrochemistry, materials characterisation, and component interaction analysis are entirely orthogonal to human-centred XR, immersive learning, collaborative systems, and spatial cognition. The research is purely materials and analytical chemistry.

methodological_fit.rationale: While the position involves experimental characterisation and quantitative analysis, the methods (electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, NMR, electron microscopy, Raman, mass spectrometry) are specific to materials science and share no conceptual or practical overlap with user-centred XR research or HCI evaluation.

growth_value.rationale: Proficiency in electrochemical methods, NMR, microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry would not advance the researcher's capability development in human-centred immersive systems, learning design, or HCI methodology.

strategic_value.rationale: Position is embedded in the Swedish COMPEL battery initiative with multi-institutional coordination and government funding stability. However, battery characterisation is a separate research ecosystem. No strategic value for candidacy toward Aalto, TU Delft, or immersive systems doctoral programs.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Posting requires 'doctoral degree or equivalent foreign degree in Electrochemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related subject with experience in electrochemistry' completed by employment decision date. Researcher's MSc in Creative Multimedia does not satisfy this requirement. Eligibility is highly questionable.
Posting emphasises hands-on experience with NMR and/or Raman spectroscopy as preferred. Researcher has no such experience.
risks: Researcher's academic background does not align with posting requirements (chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science).
Two-year postdoc in battery characterisation would create a severe disciplinary gap from HCI/XR research, significantly damaging competitiveness for target doctoral positions.
No thematic, methodological, or supervisory alignment with researcher's core domain.
Publication record would diverge from researcher's target HCI/XR venues and communities.
